$schema: Platform-independent design-token source of truth for RusoFácilapp. Not framework-specific — reusable by the web app (via scripts/build-tokens.mjs -> src/app/tokens.generated.css) and later by a native mobile build. Direction: 'Кремль' (variant C), warm-neutral revision approved 2026-08-25. Edit this file, then run `npm run build:tokens`; never hand-edit the generated CSS.

primary._comment: 600/700 updated 2026-08-26 to the chosen indigo candidate (hue 225°, was 209°) — a genuine hue shift toward navy/indigo, not just a darker step. 50-500/800/900 are UNCHANGED, still the original hue-209 ramp — this is a deliberate, scoped edit per instruction, not a full-ramp recompute. Known gap: steps 500 and below no longer share a hue with 600/700; treat as a follow-up if the lighter steps ever need to sit next to 600/700 directly.
primary.darkText_comment: Dark-theme-only alias, NOT a scale step. primary-600 itself is only 1.74:1 on neutral-900 (#171512) as plain text/link color — fails badly ('sinks' as predicted, and confirmed unused anywhere in components until the 2026-08-26 fix — every `text-primary` call site was silently sinking in dark mode). Re-tuned 2026-08-26 from an earlier L62 candidate (#7087CD, 5.23:1 on the page background) to L74 (hue 225°, sat 48%) because #7087CD only hit 3.23:1 against the new, lighter dark-theme surface color (cards, not just the page bg) — text on a card needed to pass too, not just text on bare background. #9DADDD: 8.20:1 on background, 5.05:1 on surface. Buttons do NOT need this: white text on primary-600 fill is 10.47:1 regardless of page background (button contrast is self-contained), so button/CTA fill stays primary-600 unchanged in both themes.

dark._comment: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-26 by darkText above. The old #5B9BD5/#82B8E8 belonged to the retired hue-209 dark variant and don't match the new indigo family — not reused, not silently dropped either, replacing them with a value computed fresh for AA on the new hue.

neutral._comment: Warm cream-to-ink scale, hue ~38°, replaces the scattered #f6efdc/#fff8ec/#1b140f literals. 50, 100 and 900 are exact legacy anchors (unchanged pixels) so the existing warm background everyone likes is preserved, just named.

dark._comment: Dark-theme background/surface/foreground triad — revised 2026-08-26 after a real device report ('muddy earthy' look, invisible card borders). Root cause measured in HSL: neutral-900 (#1B140F, hue 25°/sat 29%) had drifted off the rest of the scale's consistent hue ~38° line and toward a MORE saturated, redder brown at the darkest step — the opposite of the rest of the ramp, which trends toward lower saturation as it gets lighter/darker. background/surface below continue the scale's actual hue (~38°) at low, evenly-trending saturation instead, so warmth stays barely perceptible rather than reading as dirt. foreground is UNCHANGED (F5EAD2 was already 15.2:1 on the old background, never the actual problem). surface is now its own token (previously hardcoded #241c15 directly in build-tokens.mjs, bypassing tokens.json) and given real separation from background (was 1.09:1, effectively invisible layering) — see PROGRESS.md for the full before/after contrast table.

neutral.contrastWarning500: neutral-500 (#8D7C5E) fails AA (3.8:1) for normal-size text on neutral-50; only use it for large text (>=24px / >=19px bold), icons, borders, or placeholder text. Use neutral-600 (5.7:1) for any small secondary body text.

premium._comment: Gold — the ONLY other permitted accent, and only for non-clickable value markers (crown badge, Premium/Lifetime plan card, award badges, streak flame). Hue 40°, sat ~68-75%. NEVER a button or link color — see rule in CLAUDE.md, enforced by scripts/check-tokens.mjs.

dark._comment: Brighter gold for dark backgrounds — exact legacy --brand-accent-light dark value.

premium.contrastWarning500: premium-500 (#CE9627) as TEXT directly on neutral-50 fails AA (2.5:1) — it reads fine as a badge/icon FILL, but any gold text on a light background must use premium-700 (5.2:1) or darker, not 500/600.

decorativeRed._comment: NOT a semantic-danger alias, despite sharing danger's exact hex. 19 of 21 real usages of legacy --brand-accent are decorative/positive (confetti, streak flame, streak-day card, celebration win-label, 'Popular' plan badge, audio-player active-speed pill) — pointing those at --color-danger would make a streak counter or a 'Most popular' ribbon read as an error. Same hex as semantic.danger.default is intentional (was one physical color before); the two are separate named tokens so future danger-color tuning doesn't accidentally reskin confetti, and vice versa. Only login/register error messages use semantic.danger directly.

success.contrastWarning: default (#1E8E3E) is 4.0:1 on neutral-50 — fails strict AA for normal text (needs 4.5:1), passes only for large text/icons. Use strong for small text.

warning.contrastWarning: default passes at large sizes only on neutral-50; use strong for small text. Deliberately a redder/more saturated hue (25°) than premium gold (40°) so the two are never visually confusable.

danger.contrastWarning: default is the exact legacy --brand-accent value (4.4:1 on neutral-50 — borderline, fails strict AA for normal text). Reserve default for backgrounds/icons/large UI; use strong (9.8:1) for any small danger text.

level._comment: A1-C1 badges — muted so none competes with primary. 'default' = existing LevelBadge-style fill color; 'strong' (default darkened ~40%) is the AA-safe text color to pair with 'subtle' as a badge chip background. Cool-to-warm progression preserved (easy=green, hard=red) but desaturated.
level.contrastNote: verified for a1 (6.8:1, strong-on-subtle); same 0.6x-darkening derivation applied to a2-c1 — re-verify all 5 with `npm run check:tokens` before relying on them for small text.

fontFamily._verified: PT Sans/PT Serif/PT Mono (ParaType, already loaded via next/font/google, subsets latin+cyrillic) confirmed via Google Fonts metadata API to cover unicode range 160-255 (Latin-1 Supplement: á é í ó ú ñ ü ¿ ¡, all present) and 1025-1116 (Cyrillic incl. ё). No fallback substitution risk. No font change needed — kept as-is.

fontSize._comment: Fluid, rem-bounded, clamp() between 375px and 1280px viewports (the project's own 375/768/1280 breakpoints). min/max in px for reference; 'clamp' is the literal CSS value to emit.

spacing._comment: 4px-multiple scale, rem. Matches Tailwind v4's own default spacing unit (0.25rem) exactly — this section documents/locks that scale for non-Tailwind (native) reuse, it does not change Tailwind's behavior.

shadow._comment: Consolidates 5+ near-duplicate hand-picked rgba(36,28,21,...) shadows found in the audit into one warm-tinted (neutral-900-based) scale.

migration._comment: Every legacy CSS custom property, where it goes, and why. Nothing is silently dropped.
migration.--brand: color.primary.600 — VALUE CHANGED 2026-08-26 from #2D5F8A to #253B7E (indigo hue shift, chosen candidate 3 of 3). Not byte-identical to the legacy value by deliberate design decision, unlike every other migrated token in this file. Remains the sole primary/interactive color.
migration.--brand-light: color.primary.400 (#4B89C3, unchanged hue-209 ramp) — nearest scale rung to the old #4a7ba8 hover tint. Note this is now visually inconsistent with the new primary-600/700 (different hue) — acceptable short-term per the scoped-edit instruction, flagged as a follow-up.
migration.--brand-accent: color.semantic.danger.default (#D63B2F) — identical value. The old 'accent' red becomes the danger semantic, not a second brand color.
migration.--brand-accent-light: color.premium.400 (#DBA843) — nearest scale rung to the old #e0a934 gold tint (not byte-identical; within 5/1/15 per channel).
migration.--foreground (light): kept as its own literal (#241C15), close to but not forced onto neutral-900 (#1B140F) — the two were already slightly different colors in the source; not unified without a design decision.
migration.amber-500 (raw Tailwind, pricing page): color.premium.500 (#CE9627) as FILL only; premium.700 for any text use — see contrastWarning500 above.
migration.bg-foreground (graphite CTA, pricing pag: retired as an accent entirely; becomes plain neutral text/surface. All 3 pricing CTAs converge on color.primary.600.
